page: Amazon Web Services c8i.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at 3.9 GHz, this entry-tier instance provides two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyper-threading. The processing unit features a substantial cache hierarchy, including 480 MB of L3 cache, along with modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AMX-tile, and AMX-int8. It is provisioned with 4.0 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio characteristic of compute-focused platforms.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local instance storage, requiring workloads to rely exclusively on remote block storage options. Baseline networking throughput is provisioned at 1 Gbps, and no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. Across synthetic benchmark testing, the c8i.large exhibits strong single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2142.0 and high throughput in data compression routines such as single-threaded gzip (34.3 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.34 GB/sec).

Overall aggregate multi-core and multi-threaded throughput reflect the limitations of a single physical core, scoring in the lower quartiles for multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU ratings, and Clang compilation speeds. Similarly, large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks remain modest due to the narrow compute footprint. Consequently, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for lightweight compute tasks requiring modern instruction sets, high single-core clocks, or AMX matrix acceleration, while remaining constrained for memory-intensive datasets or high-concurrency multi-threaded workloads.

Workload fit is best aligned with single-threaded utilities, microservices, light build stages, lightweight batch scripting, and small edge-scale machine learning inference tasks, such as small-model prompt evaluation and text generation leveraging its AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets.

Configured with two dedicated vCPUs spanning a single physical core and paired with 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, it incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX alongside a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance excludes bundled local storage and GPUs, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations reflect strong single-core performance, evidenced by high marks in Geekbench single-core tests and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression. However, aggregate multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth are limited by the single-core footprint. The c8i.large is well-suited for lightweight compute tasks, microservices, build automation, and entry-level CPU-based inference workloads benefiting from dedicated high-frequency cores.
